When a Supabase project shows up as **“paused”**, it means the free‑tier quota has been hit and Supabase has stopped the **running services** (Postgres, Auth, Storage, etc.) so you can’t use the project right now.  
The data itself – the tables, files, Auth users, etc. – stays in your project’s storage. It just isn’t accessible until the project is resumed.

**How to get it working again**

1. **Check your email** – Supabase typically sends a message explaining why it paused and what you can do next (e.g., add a credit card, upgrade, or delete unused resources).
2. **Log in to the Supabase dashboard**  
   * Click the “Resume” button if it’s available.  
   * You’ll be prompted to add a credit card or upgrade to a paid plan. You only need to add a card; you can cancel later if you don’t want to keep the project running.
3. **Verify the data**  
   * Once resumed, go to the *Database* tab and run a simple `SELECT 1;` or look at your tables.  
   * In *Storage*, check that your files are still there.

**What will happen if you don’t resume**

- Your project will stay paused and will not accept any API calls or webhooks.  
- Supabase will eventually **delete the project after a period of inactivity** (typically 30 days). If you want to keep it, you must resume or upgrade before that time.

**Key safety note**

Adding a credit card is only for enabling the project again; you can cancel the subscription afterward if you don’t need a running backend. Your data is not deleted until you let the project stay paused for the deletion window.

So, your data is **not gone yet** – it’s still in Supabase. Just resume the project (you’ll need a card) and it will be back online. If you decide you don’t need it, delete it manually from the dashboard to avoid any future charges.
